Get It Right the First Time in association with Murmrr is thrilled to welcome back Brasswick: An Urban Brass Band Festival for the fifth consecutive year!
Brasswick, New York City’s premier music festival featuring brass bands and brassy music returns to Industry City for year seven! Join us at the Bandshell in Courtyard 1/2 for a day filled with music and fun. Hosted and headlined by Brooklyn’s own L Train Brass Band, this year’s festival will include Funkrust Brass Band, PRIZILLA, Purple Gravy, The Funky Dawgz, and The L Train Brass Band!
End the night with a NOLA-style Jam Session open to all musicians following L Train’s set. Bring your horn, drum, or whatever else makes noise. All skill levels welcome!
The venue is located in an open-air courtyard featuring a full concert sound stage. Fans can order Hometown BBQ. Additional food and drinks made at Industry City will be available for purchase. Concert is rain or shine.
Brasswick 2026 is made possible by public funds from the Greater New York Arts Development Fund of the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs, the Statewide Community Regrants Program, as well as from a regrant program of the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of the New York State Legislature, both administered by Brooklyn Arts Council
Tickets
$19.99 in advance, $25 (cash/card/Venmo) at the door.
All proceeds go directly back to supporting the festival and paying the bands. Kids under 12 enter for free with a ticketed adult.
How to get here:
Take the D, N, R lines to 36th street station in Brooklyn and walk west one block to Industry City. 2 stops from Manhattan.
From Long Island, take the LIRR to Atlantic Terminal then take the D, N, or R train from Atlantic Terminal to 36th Street! It’s 8 minutes on the subway.

events.title: Yool Kim Exhibition: Open Reception
events.description:
Open Reception Sept 12th 3 – 6pm!
Court Tree Collective is proud to present “The Place Memory Keeps,” the fourth New York City solo exhibition by Yool Kim. Building upon the emotional language that has come to define her practice, this new body of work ventures further into the quiet, dreamlike spaces where memory, longing, and imagination converge.
Kim’s paintings are driven by a continual pursuit of images that resonate on a deeply human level. Her figures and landscapes exist between reality and recollection, inviting viewers into intimate moments that feel both familiar and otherworldly. Each composition is imbued with a sense of stillness and emotional depth, revealing a painter committed to creating works that speak as much to the soul as they do to the eye.
While rooted in the timeless traditions of painting, Kim’s practice embraces a distinctly contemporary sensibility. She balances classical aesthetics with modern techniques, creating luminous surfaces and nuanced compositions that feel both enduring and unmistakably of the present. In The Place Memory Keeps, she continues to refine this visual language, offering a collection of paintings that linger long after they are seen works that remind us how memory shapes not only the places we have been, but the people we become.
